findings.reasoning: In `refund.ts`: `appendLedgerEntry(conn, {...})` is called without `await` even though the function signature changed to `Promise<void>` and now performs `await conn.query("insert into ledger ...")`. findings.claim: Batch refund notification loop has no error handling: if mailer.send fails for one row, the loop stops and remaining rows are not notified.
findings.reasoning: The notifyRefunds function (lines 11-22) loops through rows and calls await mailer.send (line 16). If this call fails for row N, the exception propagates out of the loop and function, and rows N+1 onward are never processed. The function either completes all notifications or stops partway through with no way to know which rows succeeded. If a transient network failure occurs mid-loop, the caller has no visibility into which customers got notified and which did not.

The function either completes all notifications or stops partway through with no way to know which rows succeeded. If a transient network failure occurs mid-loop, the caller has no visibility into which customers got notified and which did not.
